sections.h2: What should a Boone County seller know about the county itself?
sections.html:
Boone County sits in far northern Illinois along the Wisconsin line and belongs to the Rockford metro area. It was formed on March 3, 1836, out of Winnebago County, takes its name from Daniel Boone, and uses Belvidere as its seat and largest city. The county covers about 282 square miles in nine townships: Belvidere, Bonus, Boone, Caledonia, Flora, Leroy, Manchester, Poplar Grove and Spring.

Interstate 90, US 20 and Illinois routes 76 and 173 carry most traffic. Besides Belvidere, the incorporated places include Poplar Grove, Cherry Valley, Capron, Caledonia and Timberlane, plus the Candlewick Lake community. School districts that reach into the county are Belvidere 100, Harvard 50, Hiawatha 426, North Boone 200 and Rockford 205, so the district named on a tax bill varies by address.

  • Census estimate for July 2025: 53,568 residents, up 0.2% from the April 2020 base.
  • Owner-occupied rate of 81.8% and a median owner-occupied value of $216,900 (2020 to 2024).
  • Median gross rent of $1,041 and median household income of $84,571.
  • Mean commute of 26.6 minutes, longer than in most Illinois counties outside the Chicago area.

sections.h2: Which Boone County offices send and collect the bill?
sections.html:
Three offices share the work, and all of them sit on the Boone County Administration Campus at 1212 Logan Avenue in Belvidere. The Assessment Office (Supervisor of Assessments) is in Suite 101 and answers exemption and assessment questions at 815-544-2958. The Treasurer, in Suite 104, mails and collects bills and can be reached at 815-544-2666. The County Clerk lists real property and handles delinquent tax redemption.

The county's own overview describes a six-step cycle: the Clerk lists the property, the township assessor values it as of January 1, the county office equalizes townships to one-third of market value, the Board of Review hears complaints, the Clerk calculates rates, and the Treasurer bills and collects. A buyer or seller who understands that order knows which window is still open.

sections.h2: When is Boone County property tax due, and how can I pay it?
sections.html:
Boone County bills are normally mailed in late April and are payable in two installments, due June 1 and September 1. The treasurer says both can be paid on or before June 1, and state law has no provision for partial payments.

  • At nearly any bank in the county, bringing the whole bill if you want it stamped as proof.
  • By mail, with a check to the Boone County Treasurer postmarked on or before the due date.
  • Through your bank's bill-pay service, using the property number as the vendor account number.
  • Online by card or e-check, with convenience fees of up to 2.5% added at checkout.
  • At the Logan Avenue office with cash, check, cashier's check or money order, weekdays from 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

The treasurer does not take cards in the office or by phone. If a mortgage escrow pays your tax, check the payment status on the treasurer's website shortly before the due date and call the lender if it is still open.

sections.h2: How does a Boone County assessment appeal work?
sections.html:
You file a written complaint with the Boone County Board of Review within 30 days after assessment changes are published, or by September 10, whichever is later. The Board of Review is part of the Assessment Office, which supplies the forms.

A complaint about value has to state your opinion of market value as of January 1 of the assessment year, with proof. The county lists a closing statement for a recent purchase, at least three sales of comparable properties within one year of the assessment date, a recent appraisal, and income and expense statements for investment property. A complaint of unequal treatment needs the address, parcel number and assessed value of three or more comparison properties.

The Board sends a tentative notice, and an owner who disagrees contacts the Assessment Office within the stated time to schedule a hearing. After the Board's final notice, an owner has 30 days to appeal to the Illinois Property Tax Appeal Board in Springfield, and Circuit Court review follows after that.

sections.h2: What exemptions and limits reduce a Boone County tax bill?
sections.html:
The Assessment Office administers the homestead exemptions and the preferential assessments. As that office prints them:

  • General homestead: the rise in equalized value above 1977, up to $6,000, for an owner-occupied home.
  • Senior citizens: $5,000 off equalized value for owners 65 or older, with the first application filed with the county assessment officer.
  • Senior assessment freeze: household income under $75,000 for 2025 (payable 2026), filed every year on form PTAX-340.
  • Homestead improvement: up to $75,000 of added value, for four years.
  • Disabled persons: $2,000 off equalized value.
  • Veterans with disabilities: $2,500 at 30% to 49%, $5,000 at 50% to 69%, and all value up to $250,000 at 70% or more.

Boone County's treasurer also points out that the Property Tax Extension Limitation Law holds each taxing district's yearly increase to the lesser of 5 percent or inflation, plus new construction. The county's page notes that this is not a cap on any single bill, because assessments and exemptions can still move an individual total.

sections.h2: What happens if a Boone County tax bill goes unpaid?
sections.html:
The treasurer's page lays out the sequence below, measured from the second installment date. It describes the figures as approximate, because state statute controls them.

Unpaid-tax timeline in Boone County (source: Boone County Treasurer)
WhenWhat happens
One day after the deadlineA 1.5% penalty attaches, then 1.5% more each month
About two weeks afterCertified delinquency notice and a $10.00 fee
About one month afterList of delinquent parcels printed in a local newspaper
About two months afterTax sale; investors pay the tax plus about $44.00 in fees
Within 4 1/2 months of sale"Take notice" mailed by the County Clerk
About 2 1/2 years after saleRedemption ends and the buyer may petition for a tax deed

The redemption rate is set at the sale and can reach 18% per six months. After a sale, redemption is made through the County Clerk with cash, cashier's check or money order, and no installment plan is allowed. Title does not change at the sale itself.

sections.h2: Who pays the Boone County tax bill when the house sells?
sections.html:
The treasurer says the usual practice is for the seller to credit the buyer at closing for accrued tax, which makes the buyer responsible for the next bill. Boone County also warns that the legal remedy for unpaid tax is a lien on the property, so a new owner should confirm the earlier tax was paid.

Because tax is billed in arrears, a house sold in the fall still has an unbilled bill to come. Put the credit in writing, read the settlement statement line by line, and ask the treasurer's office for a status check on the parcel before you sign.

faqs.q: Is there a deadline to appeal a Boone County assessment?
faqs.a: Yes. The Board of Review accepts complaints within 30 days after assessment changes are published or by September 10, whichever is later. After the Board rules, you have 30 days to go to the Property Tax Appeal Board.

faqs.q: Can I pay Boone County property tax in two parts?
faqs.a: Yes, in the two installments due June 1 and September 1. The treasurer states that state law gives no room for partial payments toward a single installment, so each half must be paid in full.

faqs.q: Do I pay a fee to use a card for Boone County tax?
faqs.a: Online card or e-check payments carry convenience fees of up to 2.5%, shown at checkout. The treasurer's office cannot accept cards in person or by phone.

faqs.q: What does the Boone County Clerk do after a tax sale?
faqs.a: The Clerk takes redemption payments in certified funds and, on behalf of the tax buyer, mails the take-notice letter within about 4 1/2 months of the sale. No installment plans are accepted.

faqs.q: Where is the Boone County Assessment Office?
faqs.a: It is on the Boone County Administration Campus at 1212 Logan Avenue, Suite 101, in Belvidere, open weekdays from 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. The phone number is 815-544-2958.
